candidates.api_shape: tilt_hammer(helve_len, head_mass_box, lobes, phase_deg) -> {helve, head, wiper} third-order, 507 #72
candidates.fdm: A pivoted bar, a head, a lobed wiper. Prints. Pose is cam angle; after the lobe the head is in free flight. Teaching / hobby forge cell.
candidates.name: tilt_hammer
candidates.why: The trip-hammer primitive. snail_cam is a drop-off plate with no helve. slider_crank is constrained. This is lift-then-fall.

candidates.api_shape: drop_stamp(ram_h, wiper_n, lift, phase_deg) -> {ram, way, wipers} 507 #85
candidates.fdm: A vertical ram in a way, n wipers on a shaft. Prints. Gravity drop. Ore stamper / pulverizer cell.
candidates.name: drop_stamp
candidates.why: Vertical gravity stamp. Not a tilt (no helve) and not a press (the ram flies). 507's named ore-stamper.

candidates.api_shape: pile_release(hook_len, slot_w) -> {hooks, weight_eye, slot} opens at TDC, 507 #251
candidates.fdm: Two hooks, a slot that squeezes them. Prints. The winch is already in-tree; this is the dump.
candidates.name: pile_release
candidates.why: Automatic release at height. Not a cam (no lobe) and not a tilt. Pile-driver / drop-weight cell. The rig is a product.

candidates.api_shape: same kit, pivot between head and wiper, 507 #353
candidates.fdm: A first-order lever helve. Prints. After tilt_hammer this is an argument (order=1), not a second module.
candidates.name: trip_hammer_first_order
candidates.why: 507's other named helve. Distinct pivot. Do not ship a second name if tilt_hammer can take order=1|3.

candidates.api_shape: board_drop(board_w, ram, clutch) -> two boards + ram; friction lift, dump on release
candidates.fdm: Two boards, a ram, TPU pads. Prints as a teaching analog. Real shops use hardwood + a clutch.
candidates.name: board_drop
candidates.why: Friction lift, no cam. The other industrial drop. Distinct from drop_stamp (wipers) and from pile_release (hooks).

candidates.name: snail_as_hammer
candidates.why: A drop-off plate. usecase already names trip hammers. The missing part is the helve, not a second snail.

candidates.name: linear_cam_as_hammer
candidates.why: A translating wedge. The lift, not the falling mass. Do not claim it twice.

candidates.name: slider_crank_punch
candidates.why: Constrained punch. No free flight. Presses own it.

candidates.fdm: A piston, a valve, a frame. Nasmyth product.
candidates.name: steam_hammer_product
candidates.why: 507 steam hammer 47 is a finished machine. The cell would be a double-acting cylinder, already rejected as a product on the fluid slice.

candidates.name: forge_product
candidates.why: A smithy. The reusable part is tilt_hammer.

rejected.name: atmospheric_hammer
rejected.why: 507 #471 is a pneumatic product. Out of FDM scope as a working cell.

summary:
An impact cell stores energy (gravity or a spring) and dumps it in one stroke. 507 splits the family by how the mass is lifted and how it is released: tilt/trip hammer 72 (wiper cam lifts a third-order helve, gravity drops it), 353 (same cam, first-order helve), drop/stamp 85 (two wipers lift a vertical rod, the rod falls), pile-driver releasing-hook 251 (hooks open at the top of a slot). Norton and forge practice add the board-drop (friction boards lift the ram; a clutch dumps it) and the steam/air hammer (a piston, a product). Reuleaux's wrapping/cam higher pair is the lift; the drop is a free prismatic. This is not a press (toggles-presses: force without flight) and not a cam profile (the cam is already in-tree).

Catalog already has the lift cam, not the hammer. snail_cam usecase names trip hammers; the solid is a drop-off plate, no helve. plate_cam / roller_follower can lift; they do not fall. cams-indexing proposed linear_cam as a trip-hammer form (the translating wedge), still no hammer. Grep of mechlib/ finds no tilt_hammer, drop_stamp, or pile_release. Neighbours: slider_crank (constrained punch), toggle_joint (proposed, force lock), ratchet (holds, does not drop). A forge, a steam hammer, or a pile-driving rig is a product.

FDM reality. tilt_hammer is a pivoted helve, a head, and a wiper wheel (n lobes); pose is cam angle, the head flies after the lobe lets go. Prints as bars + a cam. drop_stamp is a vertical ram in a way, two wipers, gravity return; 507 #85 ore stamper. pile_release is a pair of hooks that a slot squeezes open at TDC; the mass falls; the lift can be a winch already in-tree. board_drop is two boards, a ram, a friction clutch; prints as a teaching analog (TPU pads). Do not emit a Nasmyth steam hammer or a smithy.
title: Trip hammers, drops, and impact cells
